protocol.admission: Dynamic structure is a candidate, not automatically accepted. Report actual quality, retention, full lifecycle CPU/wall/RSS integral, storage and selection cost against every comparator. A positive result requires better quality with no retention regression and no higher measured total cost, or an explicitly reported Pareto tradeoff; no threshold is retuned on evaluation outcomes.
protocol.evaluation_contract: Train all arms before the evaluator opens the existing held-expression artifact. This is an exploratory reuse of a published held set, not a new blind holdout. Canonical and held-expression results are reported separately; seeds and wording groups are the units, not individual repeated rows.
protocol.information_contract: Identical parent checkpoints, frozen encoder and shared frozen head; identical prefix records, replay rows and explicit entity addresses. Dynamic receives no held outcomes. Fixed graph is a serial pair of rank-4 residual operators, not a planner alias. All four structures have 10764 total and 6144 trainable parameters.
protocol.initial_equivalence: Identical typed outputs and float32 allclose rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-5; partitioning a minibatch may select a different BLAS reduction order. Record actual maximum absolute logit error. Checkpoint restore uses the same batch shape and requires exact equality.
protocol.resource_contract: One pinned CPU per training process; arms run sequentially. Matched exposure uses identical sampled row schedules. CPU-budget runs charge gradient selection and optimizer initialization against each phase allowance. Final minibatch, persistence, reload, diagnostics and interpreter startup are measured separately and included in reported lifecycle cost; a phase allowance is not a claim of an exact total-lifecycle cap.
protocol.retention_contract: Three predeclared updates change two reserves, one pack value and one limit. Every stage evaluates changed and unchanged entities, earlier updates and untouched original facts. Replay costs are included.
protocol.scope: Finite authored inventory memory with one possible split into two experts and training-only dynamic routing; no claim of recursive open-ended growth, new-entity understanding, full-agent capability, or AGI.
